1|# Install Expertery v0
2|
3|Expertery v0 is a command-line product a company installs into its OWN
4|Modal cloud account: its past work, exams and trained model stay in
5|that account. v0 supports one tool: CadQuery CAD.
6|
7|## Install
8|
9|Needs Python 3.12+, `uv`, and `modal` (run `modal setup` first).
10|
11|```sh
12|./install.sh
13|expertery init
14|```
15|
16|`install.sh` checks `uv` and `modal` exist, runs
17|`uv tool install --editable "<repo dir>"`, then prints the next step
18|(`expertery init`). It never asks for or prints secrets.
19|
20|`expertery init` checks the Modal token works (`modal profile
21|current`), reports whether a reader key is configured
22|(`EXPERTERY_READER_KEY`, falling back to `BASETEN_API_KEY`;
23|present/missing only, values are never printed), ensures the CAD box
24|app exists in the current Modal account (looks up `forge-cq`,
25|creating it if missing; no `modal deploy` step), and writes
26|`~/.expertery/config.json` (tool `cadquery`; reader url/model
27|defaults from the factory teacher, overridable via
28|`EXPERTERY_READER_URL` / `EXPERTERY_READER_MODEL` so a company can
29|point at its own Spark Open or Glimmer server). The referee (grader)
30|is ephemeral: it starts on demand during each run and stops after.
31|
32|## Privacy model (what runs where)
33|
34|- Past work, exams and the trained model live in the company's own
35|  Modal account. Nothing leaves it except reader API calls.
36|- Reader calls (Meta Muse Spark Open by default, or the company's own
37|  server via `EXPERTERY_READER_URL`) see ONLY the request text, plus
38|  the reference part's measurements in the explainer call. They NEVER
39|  see reference code (`part.py` is only built in the company's cloud
40|  box and graded by its cloud grader).
41|- Reference programs are trusted company code and build inside the
42|  locked cloud box; model answers always run in a fresh locked
43|  sandbox, never on a laptop.
44|
45|## Commands
46|
47|All examples assume the demo past work in `examples/past-work-brackets`
48|(one folder per job: `request.txt` + `part.py`).
49|
50|```sh
51|# 1. Turn past work into exam candidates ($ cap required).
52|expertery exam build examples/past-work-brackets --out results/my-exam \
53|  --cap-dollars 5 --readers 2 --workers 4
54|
55|# 2. Decide every FLAGGED job (accept / keep / drop / edit).
56|expertery exam review results/my-exam
57|expertery exam review results/my-exam --accept-all   # scripts/tests
58|
59|# 3. Lock the exam (writes exam.jsonl + FREEZE.txt).
60|expertery exam lock results/my-exam
61|
62|# 4. Run the exam on the trained or the base model ($ cap required).
63|expertery test --exam results/my-exam/exam.jsonl --model trained \
64|  --name final --out results/my-run --cap-dollars 5 --k 3
65|expertery test --exam results/my-exam/exam.jsonl --model base \
66|  --name base --out results/my-run-base --cap-dollars 5 --loop
67|
68|# 5. Serve the trained model.
69|expertery serve --name final
70|
71|# 6. Train on practice records ($ cap required; guarded entrypoint,
72|#    never `modal run ...::train`). Practice data in v0 comes from
73|#    the factory scripts (experiments/factory, experiments/r5).
74|expertery train --data train_records.jsonl --out my-model --cap-dollars 20
75|
76|# 7. Config, Modal apps, latest exam dirs.
77|expertery status
78|```
79|
80|Every command that can spend money takes `--cap-dollars` (required,
81|> 0) and `--dry-run` (prints the plan and the estimated spend, spends
82|nothing). Money: each model call is costed from its tokens with the
83|teacher's price constants; no new calls start once the next could
84|pass the cap; `spent_estimate` is written to the output.
85|
86|`exam review` accepts `--accept-all` / `--keep-all` for scripts and
87|tests (recorded with reviewer `"flag"`). Accepted or edited texts are
88|NOT re-checked automatically; `report.md` says to re-run
89|`exam build` on edited jobs to re-check them.
90|
91|## Honest limits (v0)
92|
93|- CadQuery only. `part.step` files are marked SKIPPED (not supported).
94|- Practice-job generation still uses the factory scripts
95|  (`experiments/factory`, `experiments/r5`); train/serve need GPU
96|  money in the user's own account.
97|- `exam build` refuses to overwrite an exam dir that has `exam.jsonl`;
98|  `exam lock` refuses while any FLAGGED job has no decision, and while
99|  any DEFERRED job (cap stopped new calls) is unfinished.
100|- A FLAGGED job is not a model failure: the wording may be read two
101|  ways. A person decides.

1|"""Cloud CadQuery box + grader (MUSE_SPEC section 1).
2|
3|Why this file exists (user decision 2026-10-29): nothing a model writes
4|may run on the Mac. Every answer runs in a fresh Modal Sandbox
5|(block_network=True, no secrets, no volumes, cpu 1, memory 1024-4096
6|MiB, 90 s box); one sandbox per answer, terminated after use.
7|
8|Image: python:3.12-slim + the libGL apt line + ``cadquery==2.8.0
9|cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1`` (the Mac's versions; the grader pins the same)
10|+ run_cq_box.py. It holds no references, jobs or expected files.
11|
12|Flow: write answer.py with sb.filesystem.write_text, run
13|``python /work/run_cq_box.py /work`` with sb.exec (60 s inside the 90 s
14|box, the baseline's speed limit), read back /work/answer.brep (bytes) +
15|/work/measure.json, then sb.terminate(). The run script takes the
16|``result`` variable (same rule as runner.run_code: Workplane gives its
17|solid) and writes the part as BREP (exact; not STEP). BREP answers over
18|20 MB are refused. The verdict and failure tags come only from the
19|grader; measure.json is for logs (the box runs untrusted code and must
20|not score itself).
21|
22|Grader: a Modal function (app ``forge-cq-grader``, cpu 1) with CadQuery
23|2.8 and checks.py baked in, plus /grader/first-test/{jobs.py,
24|expected.json} and /grader/factory/jobs.jsonl. ``grade(exam, job_id,
25|brep_bytes)`` scores first-test against expected.json exactly as
26|runner.py does; for factory it builds the job's reference program in
27|the grader and scores both ways (0.2% verdict + 1e-6 tight).
28|
29|Modal is imported lazily so the config helpers (sandbox kwargs, image
30|file list) are unit-testable offline. Tests inject a fake sandbox; any
31|test that could reach a real Modal call monkeypatches it to raise.
32|"""

35|
36|CQ_VERSION = "2.8.0"
37|OCP_VERSION = "7.9.3.1"
38|
39|CPU = 1
40|MEMORY_MIB = (1024, 4096)
41|SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_S = 90  # the box: one sandbox per answer
42|EXEC_TIMEOUT_S = 60  # the answer run inside it (the baseline's limit)
43|MAX_BREP_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024  # BREP answers over 20 MB are refused
44|
45|WORK_DIR = "/work"
46|ANSWER_NAME = "answer.py"
47|RUN_SCRIPT = "run_cq_box.py"  # experiments/final/run_cq_box.py, baked in
